name: Can You Compare Kitchen Remodeling Estimates Without Final Selections?

mainEntity.name: Can homeowners fairly compare kitchen remodeling estimates before choosing cabinets, countertops, and appliances?
mainEntity.text: Can homeowners fairly compare kitchen remodeling estimates before choosing cabinets, countertops, and appliances?

acceptedAnswer.text: Preliminary estimates can help establish feasibility, but they are not equal to fixed project prices when major selections remain open. Cabinets, countertops, appliances, flooring, fixtures, hardware, and lighting can change the total substantially. Ask each contractor to document a dollar allowance, quantity, product grade, and installation assumption for every undecided item. Use a selection worksheet to compare identical assumptions. Record cabinet construction, door style, finish, storage accessories, countertop material and thickness, sink, faucet, backsplash, appliance dimensions, flooring, and lighting. Confirm whether design services, delivery, installation, taxes, and disposal are included. If one contractor has detailed selections and another uses a single broad allowance, the totals are not truly comparable. Before signing, finalize the largest cost drivers whenever possible. If that cannot happen, request a range showing low, expected, and high outcomes and identify the date by which selections must be approved. Ask how price changes are documented and whether substitutions require written approval. A transparent preliminary estimate is useful, but treating it as a guaranteed final cost creates avoidable budget risk.
acceptedAnswer.description: You can compare preliminary estimates, but the comparison is limited when major selections are unresolved. Require written allowances, quantities, product assumptions, and installation terms for every undecided item. Finalize high-cost selections before signing whenever possible to reduce budget changes.
